strings.การอ่านหมายเลขโทรศัพท์ ให้อ่านแบบเรียงตั: Telephone numbers are read digit by digit. Originally, the number 2 was read as โท (tho) so that the sounds of “2” and “3” would be distinct, since telephone numbers consist of many digits and sometimes several 2s and 3s appear in sequence, and the sounds of "2" and "3" are similar. Later, as telephone systems improved greatly and “2” was no longer confused with "3", the digit "2" in telephone numbers came to be read as สอง (song), for example: 0 2225 8622 is read สูน สอง-สอง-สอง-ห้า แปด-หก-สอง-สอง (sun song-song-song-ha paet-hok-song-song)

The Three Seals Law is a compilation of Thai laws from the Ayutthaya period, which King Rama I ordered to be categorized and revised; it has been in use for over 500 years and shows the historical evolution of Thailand in politics, government, economy, society, arts and culture. As the only existing set, it is irreplaceable and therefore important at both national and global levels

strings.๑. คำในภาษาไทยที่ออกเสียงว่า บัน สามารถเ: 1. Thai words pronounced "ban" can be written in several ways, such as บรร, บัน and บรรณ, because each word has a different origin and is formed differently. 2. Words with บรร may come from Khmer, e.g. บรรทม (banthom) from ผทํ; from Sanskrit and Pali, e.g. บรรถร (banthon) from Pali ปตฺถร and Sanskrit ปฺรสฺตร; or may be derived from Thai words, e.g. บรรสาน (bansan) derived from ประสาน (prasan). Learners should consult dictionaries and academic texts on the Thai language and remember the origin or derivation of each word
strings.๑. ชื่อ “ปุณชรัศมิ์” แยกศัพท์ได้เป็นคำว่: 1. The name “ปุณชรัศมิ์” (Punnacharat) can be broken down as: - “ปุณ” from Pali “ปุณฺณ”, meaning full - “ช” from Pali and Sanskrit, meaning born - “รัศมิ์” from Sanskrit “รศฺมิ”, meaning light. Therefore, “ปุณชรัศมิ์” can be translated as “light born in fullness”. 2. The name “ปุญชรัสมิ์” (Punyacharat) can be broken down as: - “ปุญ” from Pali “ปุญฺ?”, meaning merit - “ช” from Pali and Sanskrit, meaning born - “รัสมิ์” resembles a word of Pali and Sanskrit origin, but it was not found in Pali or Sanskrit dictionaries. Since not every part of the name “ปุญชรัสมิ์” can be given a meaning, the name as a whole cannot be interpreted
